Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

on the last line of your reply:

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Task test: 21x28 binary background (0/1), with a 7 marker motif at rows 7-11, cols 23-26 (0-based). Marker positions: (7,23)=7, (8,23)=7,(8,24)=7,(9,25)=7,(10,26)=7,(11,26)=7. Eight demos requested; eight submissions wrong.

Demos strongly share a general rule with other ARC instances: a contiguous multicolor stencil/object contains one distinctive marker color that occurs elsewhere as scattered singleton target markers. Each scattered instance should be replaced/expanded by a translated copy of the stencil, aligning the marker occurrence with the corresponding marker-colored cell of stencil; preserve background and original stencil. This is NOT flood fill, not color-zeros globally, and not diagonal periodic fill. In this task the likely stencil is the 5x4 area around the connected marker structure, and each isolated 7 elsewhere should receive stencil translation anchored at same relative marker pixel(s). However exact stencil extent/anchor multiplicity not inferred in-session; do not reuse failed flood-fill/speculative outputs.

Evidence across demos: Demo1 seed color3 formed a compact polyomino and output added 3s at repeated translated instances. Demo2 likewise. Demo3/4/5 show the same colored motif repeated over random backgrounds, preserving background cells, not painting all background of a region. Demo6: seed 2 shape in rows 18-23 copied at each isolated occurrence. Demo7: a 1-pixel marker embedded in a distinctive shape; repetitions appear at many targets. Demo8: 7 seed motif at upper-left gets repeated in other positions; output changes only cells matching stencil's non-background mask and leaves background and obstacles unchanged. Test has marker 7 motif in upper-right and noise matrix of 0/1. Output should likely copy non-background stencil pixels (color 7) onto occurrences of target marker color? But targets are same color 7 only; input displayed just motif with no other 7 singletons.
